The Gemma B70 decode benchmark evaluates autoregressive throughput and latency under varying sequence lengths. To establish a reliable benchmark, the test utilizes a fixed KV cache size to isolate decoding performance from prefill overhead. This benchmark measures tokens per second (TPS) across multiple batch sizes to identify the memory bandwidth bottleneck inherent in the benchmark. 

In this benchmark, the B70 architecture demonstrates high compute utilization during the benchmark execution. As the benchmark progresses, the benchmark results indicate that memory bandwidth, rather than TFLOPS, limits the benchmark score. A critical component of the benchmark is the precision of the benchmark measurements, ensuring the benchmark captures transient fluctuations in GPU utilization. 

The benchmark concludes by comparing the benchmark metrics against baseline models. This benchmark confirms that the B70 model optimizes the benchmark-to-latency ratio. Ultimately, the benchmark serves as a standardized benchmark for assessing large-scale decoder efficiency.
